facts.text: Fredonia was founded in 1835 as a voting precinct midway between stagecoach stops at Princeton and Salem, then renamed in 1837 after founder Harvey W.’s daughter.
In 1887 the Ohio Valley Railroad ran just half a mile west of Fredonia, linking the town to the regional rail network.
The 1890s-era Fredonia Cumberland Presbyterian Church, a historic landmark listed on the National Register of Historic Places, stands as a testament to the town’s heritage.
Fredonia’s surroundings are shaped by the nearby Pennyrile State Forest, whose diverse flora and fauna influence the local ecology.
The town’s economy remains rooted in agriculture, with small businesses thriving alongside farms that benefit from fertile soils and reliable moisture.
Fredonia lies within Kentucky’s Western Coal Field physiographic province, a region known for its coal deposits and rolling landscapes of Pennsylvanian sedimentary rocks.
